verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Two routine rewritings. (a) Packaging: Lean's `energy u v t = cubeIntegral (fun x => ‖(u-v)(t,x)‖^2)` is ‖w‖²_{L²(T³)} on the unit cube, `energyRate` is its t-derivative (energy_hasDerivAt, line 590), and `dissipation (u-v) t` is ‖∇w‖²_{L²}. Halving energy_balance and adding neg_coupling_le_energy gives ½·(d/dt)‖w‖² + dissipation = -coupling ≤ B·‖w‖², which is the display with B = sup over the cube of the operator norm ‖∇u‖, i.e. ‖∇U‖_∞. energy_balance is an exact identity, hence stronger than the inequality. (b) Viscosity: the file's `navierStokesResidual` is at viscosity exactly one (ProblemStatement.lean:81), so the dissipation coefficient is 1 and not ν; the general-ν statement the paper writes is obtained in the repository by the explicit change of variables in PeriodicViscosityUniqueness (rescale ν⁻¹ ν⁻¹, normalize_residual), which yields the ν-uniqueness the paper's Gronwall sentence is used for. No declaration was found carrying a ν-weighted dissipation term in a periodic difference-energy inequality; separately, `energy_rate_le` discards the dissipation term (it keeps only energyRate ≤ 2B·energy), which is weaker than the display but is all Gronwall needs.
